activity.notes: Traditional biography identifies Sun Wu (Sun Tzu) as a general serving King Helü of Wu and associates him with Wu's victory over Chu at Boju in 506 BCE. Modern scholarship substantially disputes whether the biographical Sun Wu existed and whether the Art of War belongs to the Spring and Autumn period. ATLAS therefore records only the traditional 506 BCE military association, marks Person historicity and Activity confidence disputed, and does not fabricate a longer career interval. This request deliberately reuses the existing Spring-and-Autumn polity Wu / 오나라 already represented by King Helü (514–496 BCE); it is distinct from the later Three Kingdoms polity Eastern Wu / 동오.

sources.title: Sun Zi (Sun Tzu) (ca. fourth century BCE) — The Encyclopedia of War
sources.citation_text: The Encyclopedia of War describes Sun Zi as the purported author of the Art of Warfare, notes that many scholars doubt that such a person existed as early as the traditional Spring and Autumn setting, and records the tradition that Sun Wu served the king of Wu around 500 BCE.

sources.title: Sun Wu — Chinese Text Project
sources.citation_text: Chinese Text Project summarizes Sima Qian's later traditional biography in which King Helü appoints Sun Wu as a general and associates him with Wu's victory at Boju in 506 BCE, while also documenting long-standing doubts about his historicity.
